sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: The Tempest plugins can be used from other plugins (Java) and from content mods that have no code (JSON assets). Core is the base: everything shared is in com.atomictempest.core (events, leaderboards, help, settings, HUD lines, perks, and the economy bridge). Each plugin has its own small api package. Plugin Manifest id API Core AtomicTempest:Core com.atomictempest.core ( economy.Economies , events, leaderboards, help, settings, HUD lines, perks) Coins AtomicTempest:Coins com.atomictempest.coins.api.CoinsAPI (what only Coins has), CoinStacks Quests AtomicTempest:Quests com.atomictempest.quests

sections.title: Checklist
sections.text: Step What to do 1 Put Tempest Core (and the plugins you use) in your server's mods folder, and compile against their jars with compileOnly 2 Depend on AtomicTempest:Core in your manifest.json ; make the other Tempest plugins optional 3 Make one Registrations for your plugin and close() it in shutdown() 4 Ask Core for what you need on every use ( Economies.get() , Levels.get() ): mods can start after yours 5 Before using anything newer than the Core you support, check CoreAPI.runningVersion()

sections.title: 1. Compile against the jars
sections.text: Download the jars from the plugins' CurseForge pages, then in build.gradle : groovy Copy dependencies { compileOnly(files("libs/Core-1.5.0.jar")) compileOnly(files("libs/Quests-1.4.0.jar")) // only if you use it } compileOnly means the jars are not packed into yours: the server loads them from its mods folder.

sections.title: 2. Declare the dependencies
sections.text: json Copy "Dependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Core": "*" }, "OptionalDependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Coins": "*", "AtomicTempest:Quests": "*" } Note With an optional dependency, check that the plugin is there ( QuestsAPI.isAvailable() , CoinsAPI.get() != null ) and touch its classes in one class of yours only, so your plugin still loads without it.

sections.title: 3. Register with Core
sections.text: java Copy public class DragonsPlugin extends JavaPlugin { private final Registrations core = new Registrations("Dragons"); public DragonsPlugin(JavaPluginInit init) { super(init); } @Override protected void setup() { core.placeholder("dragons_slain", uuid -> String.valueOf(slain(uuid))); core.onAction((player, action, amount) -> { if (action.equals(PlayerActions.CRATE_OPEN)) { /* a crate was opened */ } }); } @Override public void shutdown() { core.close(); // takes back everything registered above super.shutdown(); } }

sections.title: 4. Pay a player, read their level
sections.text: java Copy Economy money = Economies.get(); // null while no economy is installed if (money != null) { money.deposit(player, 250, "Dragons: a dragon slain"); // the reason shows in the economy log } Levels.Leveling leveling = Levels.get(); // Endless Leveling or MMO Skill Tree, or null if (leveling != null && leveling.level(player) >= 20) { leveling.giveXp(player, 100, "Dragons: a dragon slain"); }

sections.title: 5. Check the Core version
sections.text: java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 19 && Skills.available()) { int mining = Skills.level(player, "Mining"); // MMO Skill Tree skills (API 19) } Tip Keep code that needs a newer Core in a class of its own and call it only after the check: on an older Core the class is then never loaded, and your plugin keeps working. Next: Setting up a plugin has every option, and Player actions lists everything the Tempest plugins report.

sections.title: Setting up a plugin
sections.text: Compile against the jars you use, without bundling them; the server loads them from Mods: groovy Copy dependencies { compileOnly(files("$hytaleHome/UserData/Mods/Core-1.0.0.jar")) compileOnly(files("$hytaleHome/UserData/Mods/Quests-1.1.0.jar")) // only if you use it } Download the jars from the plugins' CurseForge pages ( https://www.curseforge.com/hytale/mods/search?search=tempest ). In your manifest.json , depend on what you use so it starts before your plugin: json Copy "Dependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Core": "*" }, "OptionalDependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Coins": "*", "AtomicTempest:Quests": "*" } With an optional dependency, check CoinsAPI.get() != null or QuestsAPI.isAvailable() (or LotteryAPI.isAvailable() ...) before use, and keep the classes that touch it apart from the rest, so your plugin still loads when it is missing. Use the APIs in your plugin's setup() or later.

sections.title: The shortest way: Registrations and JsonFiles (Core)
sections.text: Registrations registers with Core's registries and remembers how to undo each one; one close() in shutdown() takes it all back, so a reload never leaves a settings tab, help page, listener or timer behind: java Copy private final Registrations core = new Registrations("Dragons"); protected void setup() { config = DragonsConfig.load(); core.settingsTab(new SettingsTab("Dragons", settings(config), config::save)); core.helpTopic(new HelpTopic("dragons", 80, Message.translation("server.dragons.help.title"), "Rock_Gem_Ruby", uuid -> lines(uuid))); core.helpCommand("server.dragons.help.mod", "/dragons", Message.translation("server.dragons.help.command")); core.hudLine("dragons.next", uuid -> Message.translation("server.dragons.hud.next")); core.placeholder("dragons_slain", uuid -> String.valueOf(slain(uuid))); core.mapKind(new MapPlaces.Kind("nest", "Dragon nests", Message.translation("server.dragons.map.nest")).blocks("Dragon_Nest"::equals)); core.leaderboard(board); core.onWallet(listener); core.veto(veto); core.onAction(listener); core.onAnnouncement(listener); core.restrictCraft("Dragon_Egg", () -> config.playersCanCraft()); core.edition(isPro, PRO_ADDS, licensedTo); // plugins with a free and a Pro jar core.every(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS, () -> spawnDragons()); // its own daemon timer thread; errors are logged core.later(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS, () -> greet()); core.onClose(() -> config.save()); // anything else for shutdown() } public void shutdown() { core.close(); // newest first;

sections.title: Which Core is installed: CoreAPI (Core)
sections.text: CoreAPI.runningVersion() is the API version of the Core on the server ( CoreAPI.API_VERSION is the one you compiled against; it is copied into your plugin, so ask runningVersion() at run time). Version 1 is Core 1.0.0. Core's stable API , safe to build on: the classes directly in com.atomictempest.core (except Main ) and the packages economy , help and settings . These only grow. Core's command , config , listener , player and ui packages and Main are internal and may change in any release; do not use them. The other plugins' APIs are their api packages ( Holograms.API_VERSION , QuestsAPI.API_VERSION , CoinsAPI.VERSION , CoinflipAPI.VERSION ...). java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() < 1) { /* a Core older than the one you built against */ }

sections.title: Reference: Core API versions
sections.text: CoreAPI.API_VERSION is the version a plugin was built against; CoreAPI.runningVersion() is the one installed on the server. Check the running version before touching anything newer than your lowest supported Core, and keep that code in a class of its own. Version Added 1 Core 1.0.0: Registrations , JsonFiles , Economies , CasinoSettings , HelpTopics , HudLines , Leaderboards , Placeholders , PlayerActions , WalletEvents and the rest of the first release 2 AdminLog , RateLimit , and settings tab groups ( tempest.admin.<group> ) 3 PlayLimits , HudLines.compact , Themes , dropdowns and item pickers in settings ( Setting.choice , Setting.item ), tab icons, ItemIcons.ids and pretty 4 The Tempest board's line names and keys ( HudLines.name , nameOf , keys , lineFor ) 5 Boosts and Registrations.boost ; PlayerActions.QUEST_COMPLETE and CONTRACT_DELIVER 6 Mailbox (/mail) and HudLines.startOff 7 MapPlaces and Registrations.mapKind 8 Unlocks and Registrations.unlockFeature , unlockProvider , onUnlock 9 Activity and Perks.highestPercent 10 Perks.Bonus.PASS_XP 11 SettingsTab.defaults (Reset to defaults) 12 JsonFiles config versions with migrations, and JsonFiles.rename 13 Doctor (/tempest doctor) and Registrations.doctor 14 Levels : player levels from a leveling mod 15 Levels dungeon, wave gate and raid clears; Boosts.LEVELING_XP 16 Levels XP, level cap, class, race, mob level, parties, raid starts, meets , hasClass , mobGold , mobKilled , playersAtLevel , serverClears , serverPrestige ;

sections.title: Money: Economies (Core)
sections.text: The server's money, whichever plugin keeps it: Coins when it is installed, otherwise any economy VaultUnlocked offers (Ecotale, TheEconomy, EliteEssentials...). Ask for it on every use: an economy can start after your plugin. java Copy Economy money = Economies.get(); // com.atomictempest.core.economy; null when there is none long balance = money.balance(uuid); money.deposit(uuid, 250, "Dragon bounty"); // false if refused; the reason shows in Coins' wallet history if (money.withdraw(uuid, 100, "Ferry ticket")) { /* paid */ } // false (nothing taken) if too little or vetoed money.has(uuid, 100); money.format(1250); // "1,250 copper", or "$1,250.00" from another economy Amounts are whole numbers of the economy's smallest unit (an economy with decimals shows balances rounded down). Always give a reason. withdraw asks the WalletEvents vetoes first, and every change through any economy reaches WalletEvents listeners. Coins the player holds as items are not in the wallet until deposited.

sections.title: Coins: CoinsAPI
sections.text: What only Coins has. CoinsAPI is also an Economy , so everything above works on it too. java Copy CoinsAPI coins = CoinsAPI.get(); // null when Coins is not installed coins.setBalance(uuid, 1000); // "Set by an admin" in the history coins.transfer(from, to, 50, "Trade"); // "Paid: Trade" / "Received: Trade" coins.paidAsCoins(uuid, 250, "Slot machine win"); // VERSION 4: you paid coin items instead of the wallet List<ItemStack> items = CoinStacks.of(1250); // coin items worth an amount, most valuable first When your plugin pays out coin items instead of money (dropped, put in a tray), call paidAsCoins with the reason you would give a wallet change: the balance does not change, but the economy screen ( /eco ) and the leaderboards count the payout under its kind. Without it the money shows up only later, as "Deposited coins". Town unlock: Coins describes the feature coins:bank_interest ("Bank savings interest") with Core's Unlocks (Core API 8) and pays savings interest only while Unlocks.isOn("coins:bank_interest") and the admin has switched it on. A plugin that decides the unlocks ( Registrations.unlockProvider ) can keep it off, for example until a bank building is finished; without one, Coins' own setting decides. Interest is paid into banks with the history line "Savings interest" (no wallet changes, so no WalletEvents ).

sections.title: Stopping payments: WalletEvents.addVeto
sections.text: A veto is asked before coins leave a wallet (bets, crates, shop purchases, payments) and can refuse with a sentence for the player. Coins coming in cannot be refused, because the player may already have handed something over for them. java Copy WalletEvents.addVeto((uuid, amount, reason) -> jail.contains(uuid) ? "You cannot spend coins in jail." : null); String why = WalletEvents.checkRemoval(uuid, 100, "Ferry ticket"); // ask first to show the reason

sections.title: Player actions
sections.text: All in com.atomictempest.core , available whether or not Coins is installed.

sections.title: Hearing about money: WalletEvents and PlayerActions
sections.text: java Copy // Every change of any wallet (after it happened) WalletEvents.listen((player, amount, reason, balanceAfter) -> { ... }); // What players do in the economy mods: spins, wins, tickets, shop trades, daily rewards, payments PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> { if (PlayerActions.SLOT_JACKPOT.equals(action)) { ... } }); // Report your own (other listeners, such as Quests, may count them) PlayerActions.fire(uuid, "mymod:bounty", 250); Actions: slot_spin (bet), slot_win (winnings, also when dropped as coins), slot_jackpot , lottery_tickets (how many), lottery_win , shop_buy (cost), shop_sell (paid), daily_reward , pay , crate_open (price), coinflip_bet (stake), coinflip_win (paid), coinflip_loss (stake), quest_complete (reward paid; Core API 5, reported by Quests for every quest and achievement finished), contract_deliver (items delivered; Core API 5, reported by Contracts for every delivery to a server order), events_top (the place, 1 to 3, when an event ends), events_helped (a goal reached and the helper paid), trade_done (to each side of a finished trade that moved something; the amount is a number that always stands for the same other player), town_mayor (elected at the end of a term). Listeners run on the thread that made the change: keep them quick, and do world or UI work with world.execute(...) .

sections.title: Reference: every player action
sections.text: Everything the Tempest plugins report through PlayerActions (Core), in one place. Listen once and count what you need; the amount means what the table says. Listeners run on the thread that reported: keep them quick and thread-safe. java Copy PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> { switch (action) { case PlayerActions.CRATE_OPEN -> ...; // a constant on PlayerActions case "jobs_level" -> ...; // the other plugins' actions are plain strings default -> { } } }); Action From Fires when Amount slot_spin ( PlayerActions.SLOT_SPIN ) Slots A slot machine spin The bet slot_win ( SLOT_WIN ) Slots A win, paid or dropped as coins The winnings slot_jackpot ( SLOT_JACKPOT ) Slots A jackpot (also reported as a win) The winnings lottery_tickets ( LOTTERY_TICKETS ) Lottery Tickets bought How many lottery_win ( LOTTERY_WIN ) Lottery A lottery win The prize shop_buy ( SHOP_BUY ) Shop Bought from the shop What it cost shop_sell ( SHOP_SELL ) Shop Sold to the shop What it paid daily_reward ( DAILY_REWARD ) Coins A daily reward claimed The reward pay ( PAY ) Coins A payment to another player What was paid crate_open ( CRATE_OPEN ) Crates A crate opened What it cost (0 when free) quest_complete ( QUEST_COMPLETE , API 5) Quests A quest or achievement finished The reward paid, 0 if none contract_deliver ( CONTRACT_DELIVER , API 5) Contracts Items delivered to a contract or server order How many items coinflip_bet ( CoinflipAPI.ACTION_BET ) Coinflip A stake put into a room The stake coinfl

sections.title: Admin settings: CasinoSettings
sections.text: java Copy CasinoSettings.register(new SettingsTab("Dragons", List.of( Setting.heading("Bounties", "What players earn for dragons."), Setting.number("Bounty", 0, 1_000_000, 0, () -> config.bounty, v -> config.bounty = (long) v) .hint("Per dragon.").preview(() -> Message.raw("= " + Currency.format(config.bounty))), Setting.toggle("Announce kills", () -> config.announce, v -> config.announce = v), Setting.text("Chat tag", true, () -> config.tag, v -> config.tag = v).icon("Weapon_Sword_Iron").caption("Tag"), Setting.color("Colour", () -> config.tagColor, v -> config.tagColor = v).inline() ), config::save)); Your tab appears in /tempest for admins (permission tempest.admin ), up to 40 settings. Staff with tempest.admin.<group> see only that group's tabs. The group is the title in lower case without spaces ( tempest.admin.dragons ); give it yourself when your plugin has more than one tab, so one permission covers them all (API 2): new SettingsTab("Dragon Loot", "dragons", settings, config::save) . Where there are only a few right answers, give admins a dropdown instead of a number or a code (API 3): java Copy Setting.choice("Difficulty", List.of(Setting.option("easy", "Easy"), Setting.option("hard", "Hard")), () -> config.difficulty, v -> config.difficulty = v), Setting.choiceNumber("Corner", List.of(Setting.option("1", "Top right"), Setting.option("2", "Left")), () -> config.corner, v -> config.corner = v), // a setting kept as a whole number Setting.item("Reward item", () -> conf

sections.title: Menu themes: Themes
sections.text: The admin picks the look of every Tempest menu ( /tempest , General, "Menu theme"): Tempest gold (the plugins' own look), Dark crimson, Elven emerald, Frostbite, Amethyst, Cyberpunk neon, Cozy parchment, or their own two colours. Use it on your pages so they match: Put your .ui files in a folder with your own name in it ( Common/UI/Custom/Pages/MyName_Dragons/ ), never straight in Pages/ or in a folder named after a feature ( Pages/Quests/ ): every mod's UI files and the game's share one folder tree in the client, and a file at the same path as another mod's replaces it. Tempest's own are in Pages/AtomicTempest_<Plugin>/ and Hud/AtomicTempest_* . java Copy cmd.append("Pages/MyName_Dragons/DragonsPage.ui"); Themes.tint(cmd, "#Content"); // the page's body in the theme's colour cmd.set("#Heading.TextSpans", Themes.accent("Bounties")); // titles and highlights Themes.row(cmd, "#List[0]"); // a row in the theme's row colour The default theme paints nothing, so a page looks as its .ui file says until an admin picks a theme.

sections.title: Free and Pro editions: Editions
sections.text: For plugins that come as a free and a Pro jar (Crates, Quests and Holograms do; yours can too). Register the edition in setup() , unregister it in shutdown() . Only admins ever see these texts. java Copy Editions.register("MyPlugin", isPro, List.of("any number of arenas", "team modes"), licensedTo); settings.add(Editions.heading("MyPlugin")); // "Free edition: the Pro edition adds ..." at the end of your /tempest tab String why = Editions.limitReached("MyPlugin", "5 arenas"); // "The free edition of MyPlugin has up to 5 arenas. ..." String what = Editions.proOnly("MyPlugin", "Team modes"); // "Team modes are in the Pro edition of MyPlugin." Editions.isPro("Crates"); // which edition another plugin runs licensedTo is shown in the Pro heading ("Licensed to ..."); pass "" when there is none. Keep your API the same in both editions, and let free limits only stop making more, never break what a server already has.

sections.title: Languages: Lang
sections.text: Texts are Hytale translation keys. Put them in src/main/resources/Server/Languages/<locale>/server.lang (prefix them with your plugin's id, so mymod.help.title = Dragons is server.mymod.help.title ), set "IncludesAssetPack": true , and send Message.translation(key).param(...) . The game fills in English for keys a language lacks. Message.raw(text) still works for text that needs no translation. java Copy String language = Lang.languageOf(playerRef); // the language the plugins use for this player String text = Lang.text(language, Message.translation("server.mymod.hud.bounty").param("amount", "250")); // for logs, signs, placeholders The admin can pick one language for everyone ( /tempest → General → Language), for languages Hytale does not offer yet (German, Italian, Polish). That only covers keys under the Tempest plugins' own prefixes.

sections.title: The help screen: HelpTopics
sections.text: java Copy HelpTopics.register(new HelpTopic("mymod", 80, Message.translation("server.mymod.help.title"), "Weapon_Sword_Iron", uuid -> List.of( HelpTopic.heading("server.mymod.help.bounties"), Message.translation("server.mymod.help.earn").param("amount", Currency.format(250)))) .button(Message.translation("server.mymod.help.open"), (player, ref, store) -> { openPage(player, ref, store); return false; })); HelpTopics.registerCommand("server.mymod.help.mod", "/bounties", Message.translation("server.mymod.help.bountiesCmd")); HelpTopics.open(playerRef, ref, store) opens the help screen (for a command like /coins ). HelpTopics.justWelcomed(uuid) is true for a minute after the help screen opened by itself for a new player: a page you would open on join should wait, so the two do not cover each other. HelpTopic.heading(key) makes a heading line (bold). Shown in /guide (and /coins with Coins) for every player.

sections.title: Leaderboards: Leaderboards
sections.text: Shown on Coins' /leaderboards (servers without Coins have no leaderboard screen; registering is still safe). java Copy Leaderboards.register(new Leaderboards.Board("mymod:dragons", Message.translation("server.mymod.board.title"), Message.translation("server.mymod.board.hint"), "server.mymod.board.count", uuid -> MyMod.dragonsKilled(uuid))); // count key: a number with its unit, "{count, plural, one {1 dragon} other {{count} dragons}}"; null = money ("1,250 copper") The board appears on /leaderboards after the built-in ones. It ranks every player Coins knows; players with 0 are left out. Unregister it in your shutdown() .

sections.title: The coin counter: HudLines
sections.text: java Copy HudLines.register("mymod:bounty", uuid -> hasBounty(uuid) ? Message.translation("server.mymod.hud.bounty").param("amount", HudLines.format(bounty(uuid))) : null); Up to three lines show under each player's coin counter; return null to show nothing. Called every two seconds from a timer thread. With the Tempest board on (Core's panel on the right of the screen), every line shows there instead, and each player picks which ones in /board . Give your line a name for that menu (API version 4): java Copy HudLines.name("mymod:bounty", Message.translation("server.mymod.board.bounty")); // "Bounty" HudLines.keys(); HudLines.nameOf(key); HudLines.lineFor(key, uuid); // API version 4 A line that is nice to have but should not push others off a full board can start off; each player switches it on in /board (API version 6; Shop's daily deal does this): java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 6) HudLines.startOff("mymod:bounty"); An economy plugin calls HudLines.moneyChanged(player, change) when a balance changes, so the counter shows the new amount and the change at once instead of at its next refresh, and HudLines.refreshMoney() after the currency's name or look changed (Coins does both).

sections.title: A progress bar on the screen: HudLines.progress
sections.text: A bar under the money counter for five seconds: an item icon, a short line and how far along (0 to 1). A newer bar replaces the one showing. Shown even while the Tempest board replaces the counter, never when the player hid it with /hud. One HUD for everything, so it never fights another mod's HUD. java Copy HudLines.progress(uuid, "Tool_Pickaxe_Iron", Message.raw("Miner 14 +6 XP"), 0.42f); HudLines.progress(uuid, "Tool_Pickaxe_Iron", Message.raw("Miner 14"), 0.42f, 8000); // shown for 8 seconds

sections.title: Announcements: Announcements
sections.text: Big moments (jackpots, big wins, lottery winners, achievements) are posted here for integrations such as the Discord webhook. Post your own: Announcements.post("mymod_boss", "Steve defeated the Dragon!") (shown in Discord when "News from other mods" is on); listen with Announcements.listen((category, text) -> ...) .

sections.title: Item and command rewards: Rewards
sections.text: The same rewards in every plugin. Admins type items as one line ( Ingredient_Bar_Iron x16, Food_Bread x5 ; 16 Food_Bread and a bare id for one work too), at most Rewards.MAX_KINDS (8) kinds and MAX_AMOUNT (1000) of each. giveItems puts them in the inventory; what does not fit, and everything for a player who is offline, waits in the mailbox. The parcel is saved before anything is given, so a crash can neither lose nor double it. Any thread. java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 18) { String problem = Rewards.itemsProblem(text); // in the editor: null when it can be saved List<Mailbox.Item> items = Rewards.parseItems(text); // the same ids added together, junk left out Rewards.describe(items); // "16 Ingredient Bar Iron, 5 Food Bread", for players Rewards.giveItems(uuid, "Dragons", "server.dragons.mail.reward", Map.of("dragon", "Ember"), items); Rewards.commandProblem(command); // one line, at most MAX_COMMAND (200) characters Rewards.runCommand(uuid, name, "cratekey give {player} vote 1"); // as the console; name null: looked up online }

sections.title: One mailbox for every plugin: Mailbox
sections.text: Instead of dropping a reward at a player's feet (full inventory) or keeping it in your own file until they come back (offline), send it to their mailbox. Players open it with /mail , are told when a parcel arrives and when they join, and see "Mail: 2" on the Tempest board. Claiming gives what fits; the rest stays in the parcel, and money is paid through the server's economy. java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 6) { String id = Mailbox.send(uuid, "Dragons", "server.dragons.mail.reward", Map.of("dragon", "%server.dragons.name.ember"), // a value starting with % is a translation key List.of(new Mailbox.Item("Rock_Gem_Ruby", 3)), 500); // items and money if (id == null) { ... } // nothing in it, or the mailbox is full (Mailbox.MAX_PARCELS): keep the reward yourself } Mailbox.count(uuid); Mailbox.of(uuid); // what is waiting The title is a key in your plugin's server.lang , so each player reads it in their language. Crates sends keys from /cratekey and key parties there when the player is not in a world.

sections.title: Boosts for a while: Boosts
sections.text: More of something for a while: monster and ore gold, daily and quest rewards, battle pass XP, shop prices. Tempest Events turns them on during an event; your plugin can too (a full moon, a boss kill, a vote party). The plugins that pay out ask for the boost at the moment they pay, in percent like Perks (100 = double). Several sources add up, to at most 1000%; a discount takes at most 90% off. java Copy core.boost("mymod:full-moon", (kind, player) -> Boosts.MOB_COINS.equals(kind) && fullMoon() ? 50 : 0); // Registrations long paid = Boosts.boosted(Boosts.MOB_COINS, killer, amount); // what Coins does for each monster long price = Boosts.discounted(Boosts.SHOP_DISCOUNT, player, price); Boosts.percent(Boosts.PASS_XP, player); // 50.0 Kind Used by What it raises MOB_COINS Coins coins a monster drops (after the admin's cap) ORE_COINS Coins coins found in ores DAILY_REWARD Coins the daily reward (after rank perks) QUEST_REWARD Quests quest and achievement rewards (after rank perks) PASS_XP Pass battle pass XP (added to the Pro weekend boost) SHOP_SELL Shop what the shop pays (never more than its buying price) SHOP_DISCOUNT Shop off the shop's prices "contract_pay" Contracts what server orders pay (players' contracts pay what their poster put up, never boosted) Your own kind: pay out through Boosts.boosted("mymod_bounty", player, amount) and describe it with Boosts.describe("mymod_bounty", Message.translation("server.mymod.boost"), "Weapon_Sword_Iron") , so Tempest Events' editor li

sections.title: Rank perks: Perks
sections.text: Admins set up to four perks in /tempest (Rank Perks tab), each tied to a permission such as coins.perk.vip , which a permissions plugin gives to a rank. Read them for your own rewards: java Copy Perks.percent(uuid, Perks.Bonus.DAILY_REWARD); // 25.0 = 25% more Perks.boosted(uuid, Perks.Bonus.QUEST_REWARD, 100); // 125 Perks.discounted(uuid, Perks.Bonus.SHOP_DISCOUNT, 100); // 90 Perks.name(uuid); // "VIP", or "" without a perk Perks are checked against the player's permissions while they are online; offline players get none. Perks.highestPercent(Perks.Bonus.SHOP_DISCOUNT) (API version 9) is the best value any perk on the server gives, whoever has it. Cap what you pay players with it, so someone with a discount cannot buy for a friend who sells back. Perks.Bonus.PASS_XP (API version 10) is a rank's pass XP bonus; Tempest Pass (Pro) adds it to every XP gain. Check CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 10 before using it.

sections.title: Places on the world map: MapPlaces
sections.text: Register a kind of place and Core does the rest: a tab in /tempest (on or off, icon, colour, name, size, compass, who sees it, how far away, which worlds), changing or hiding one place from /places , and each player picking what their map shows. java Copy // Blocks: Core remembers each one when it is placed or used, and forgets it when it goes core.mapKind(new MapPlaces.Kind("nest", "Dragon nests", Message.translation("server.dragons.map.nest")) .icon("Tempest_Star.png").color("#E74C3C").item("Rock_Gem_Ruby") .blocks(id -> id.equals("Dragon_Nest"))); // Or your own list, asked for every few seconds on any thread, so keep it quick core.mapKind(new MapPlaces.Kind("dragon", "Dragons", Message.translation("server.dragons.map.dragon")) .places(() -> dragons.stream() .map(d -> new MapPlaces.Place(d.id(), d.world(), d.x(), d.y(), d.z(), d.name())).toList())); MapPlaces.refresh(); // after a change that should show at once Kind.startOff() leaves a kind off until an admin turns it on. A place's key must stay the same, as admins' changes are kept under it. The second argument of Kind is what admins read in /tempest ; the third is what players read. Icons are files in Common/UI/WorldMap/MapMarkers , so an asset pack can add its own: MapPlaces.ICONS lists what every server has. Paint them white with a dark edge and the admin's colour tints them.

sections.title: Features the town unlocks: Unlocks
sections.text: Some features should wait until the server has earned them: savings interest once the town has a bank, market stalls once the market hall stands. Describe each such feature, and ask Core before using it: java Copy core.unlockFeature(new Unlocks.Feature("dragons:nest_rewards", "Dragon nest rewards", // Registrations Message.translation("server.dragons.unlock.nests"), "Rock_Gem_Ruby")); if (Unlocks.isOn("dragons:nest_rewards")) { payNestReward(); } core.onUnlock((feature, on) -> { if (feature.equals("dragons:nest_rewards")) refreshNests(); }); The id is your plugin's name and the feature; keep it the same, as admins' choices are kept under it. The second argument is what admins read in menus, the third what players read on /town . Without a provider every feature is on , so a server without Tempest Town works as before and your plugin's own settings decide. Tempest Town is the provider ( tempest:town ): an admin ties features to unlocks there (always on, always off, or once a building is finished, a date has come or another unlock came first). A feature no unlock names stays on. isOn is asked from any thread and answers from memory, so call it as often as you like. A listener hears a feature switched on or off on the thread that changed it. Your own provider (a plugin that decides unlocks some other way): core.unlockProvider("mymod", feature -> ...) returns TRUE , FALSE , or null to leave the feature on. A feature is off when any provider says off. Tell the plugins with Unlocks

sections.title: Items the server wants: Demand
sections.text: A plugin with orders tells Core what is wanted; any plugin asks Core, so neither depends on the other. Tempest Contracts provides the items of its open server orders (players' own contracts do not count, so a cheap one cannot raise everyone's pay); Tempest Jobs pays more for work that brings one in. java Copy core.demandSource("myplugin", () -> Set.of("Ore_Iron", "Wood_Oak_Trunk")); // removed by core.close() Demand.isWanted("Ore_Iron_Stone"); // true: the id contains a wanted id ("_Item" endings are ignored) Demand.wanted(); // every wanted id now, from every source (kept for 10 seconds)

sections.title: Who changed what: AdminLog
sections.text: Record admin changes so servers with several staff can see who did what. Lines go to universe/mods/atomictempest/admin-log/<day>.log ; /tempest log shows the newest. Line breaks in the text are removed, so a typed name cannot add a false line. java Copy AdminLog.record(player.getUsername(), "Dragons", "Bounty: 250 -> 500"); AdminLog.record(AdminLog.CONSOLE, "Dragons", "Reset every dragon");

sections.title: Stopping floods: RateLimit
sections.text: At most once in a while per key, for announcements, payments and messages a player could repeat: java Copy if (RateLimit.allow("dragons:announce:" + player, 30_000)) { announce(...); }

sections.title: A daily limit for games of chance: PlayLimits
sections.text: The admin sets one daily limit per player for every game of chance together ( /tempest , General, "Daily limit for games"; 0 = none). A game counts each stake before it takes the money, and gives it back if the money is not taken or the stake is refunded: java Copy Message stop = PlayLimits.reserve(player, bet); // counts the bet, or says why not (shown to the player) if (stop != null) { player.sendMessage(stop); return; } if (!economy.withdraw(player, bet, "Dragon dice")) { PlayLimits.release(player, bet); return; } PlayLimits.check(player, amount) says why without counting (for a price shown before buying); PlayLimits.leftToday(player) is what the player may still stake today.

sections.title: Who is really playing: Activity
sections.text: Pay for time played only to players who are there. A player counts as active while they turned their view in the last Activity.AFK_MINUTES (5) minutes; water pushing them or standing in a farm moves them but never turns their head. A player who has just joined counts as active. java Copy if (Activity.isActive(uuid)) { addMinutePlayed(uuid); } Activity.idleMillis(uuid); // how long they have not turned their view Tempest Pass (minutes played) and Tempest Events (playtime goals) use it. Check CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 9 first.

sections.title: Catching money from nothing: Doctor
sections.text: /tempest doctor looks through every plugin's settings for ways players could make money from nothing, before they find them. A plugin that pays coins or takes items for coins adds a check, and its prices take part in every check the doctor runs across plugins: java Copy core.doctor(new Doctor.Check() { // Registrations public void prices(Doctor.Market market) { // where players buy items for coins, and get coins for items, with the settings as they are now market.buy("my stall", "Ingredient_Bar_Iron", 12, 0, "/mystall"); // 0 = no daily limit market.sell("my bounty board", "Ingredient_Bar_Iron", 20, 64, "/bounties"); market.play(Doctor.CRATE_OPENS, averageLossPerOpening, "my crate"); // for quests that count openings } public void check(Doctor.Market market, Doctor.Findings findings) { long worth = market.worth("Rock_Gem_Diamond"); // the most any plugin pays for one if (myPrize > myPrice) findings.problem("prize", "My prize is worth more than it costs.", "My price"); } }); Core itself finds every item bought cheaper in one place than it sells for in another, and every game recipe whose parts, bought at their cheapest, cost less than what it makes sells for (items only admins may craft are left out). A finding is problem (money from nothing), warning (easy to farm) or hint . Its key must stay the same between checks, as the admin can mark it "on purpose". A fix is a command ( "/shop" ) or the label of a setting in /tempest, which the FIX button searches for. Texts are for adm

sections.title: Saving files safely: SafeFiles
sections.text: All six plugins save through it, and other plugins may too. A save survives a crash or power cut at any moment: the text goes to name.tmp (flushed to disk), the old file becomes name.bak , then the new one takes its place. java Copy SafeFiles.write(path, gson.toJson(data)); // throws IOException if it could not save MyData data = SafeFiles.load(path, reader -> gson.fromJson(reader, MyData.class)); // null if no copy can be read SafeFiles.exists(path); // also true if only the .tmp or .bak is left load uses the newest complete copy; a file that cannot be read is kept as name.broken-<time> and the backup is used instead.

sections.title: Other helpers
sections.text: Currency : the money's name ( format , name , singular , plural ). Use it instead of writing "copper". ChatPrefix.of(text, "#RRGGBB") : a coloured chat tag such as "[Dragons]". ItemIcons.safe(itemId) : an item id that is safe to draw; Coins' coin items fall back to similar game items when Coins is not installed. CoinStacks.of(amount) (in Coins): the coin items that make up an amount (for dropping coins). ReservedDrops.spawn(...) : dropped items only one player can pick up for a while. CraftRestrictions.restrict(itemId, () -> allowed) : admin-only crafting with an on/off switch.

sections.title: Player levels: Levels
sections.text: Player levels from whichever leveling mod the server runs, as Economies is for money: Endless Leveling or MMO Skill Tree , found by themselves through their public APIs (nothing of them is shipped). With both installed, the admin picks the one that gives "the level" on the /tempest Leveling tab. Another mod's bridge can Levels.register its own Leveling , which then comes first. java Copy Levels.Leveling leveling = Levels.get(); // null without a leveling mod if (leveling != null) { int level = leveling.level(uuid); int prestige = leveling.prestige(uuid); // 0 with MMO Skill Tree leveling.giveXp(uuid, 250, "Quest: Miner"); // with the mod's own bonuses and level cap } if (!Levels.meets(uuid, 20)) { ... } // true without a leveling mod: nobody is locked out by a missing mod Note With MMO Skill Tree, level is the number the admin chose on its tab (total, combat or power level, or the highest skill), and leveling XP goes into the skill chosen there. Its skills one by one are in Skills (below).

sections.title: Levels (static)
sections.text: Method Returns Since What it does get() Leveling 14 The leveling mod in use, or null. Asked again on every call register(leveling) / unregister(leveling) 14 A bridge for another leveling mod; it is preferred over the ones Core finds listen(listener) / stopListening(listener) 14 Hear level-ups, prestige and clears (below) available() boolean 16 A leveling mod runs level(uuid) int 16 The player's level, 0 without a leveling mod meets(uuid, minLevel) boolean 16 The player has at least this level; true without a leveling mod hasClass(uuid, wanted) boolean 16 The player's class (or second class) is this one; true without a mod or a class mobLevel(ref, store, buffer) int 16 A mob's level (Endless Leveling), 0 when not known. On the mob's world thread mobGold(amount, killer, mobLevel) long 16 Mob gold raised by the mob's level, as the admin set it mobKilled(killer, mobName, mobLevel) 16 Tell Core of a kill (elite mob announcements) playersAtLevel(level) int 16 Players seen at this level or higher (for town conditions) serverClears() / serverPrestige() long 16 Dungeons, gates and raids cleared by everyone; everyone's highest prestige added up pretty(id) String 16 "dark_knight" becomes "Dark Knight" describe() String 14 "Endless Leveling", "MMO Skill Tree" or "none" fireLevelUp , firePrestige , fireDungeonCleared , fireGateCleared , fireRaidCleared , fireRaidStarted 14-16 For a bridge: tell Core and every listener

sections.title: Levels.Leveling (one leveling mod)
sections.text: Method Returns Since What it does name() String 14 "Endless Leveling", "MMO Skill Tree" level(uuid) / prestige(uuid) int 14 Level and prestige (0 when the mod does not know the player) giveXp(uuid, amount, reason) boolean 14 XP with the mod's bonuses and cap; false when it could not xp(uuid) / xpForNext(uuid) double 16 XP toward the next level, and what it needs (0 when the mod does not say) levelCap(uuid) int 16 The highest level this player can reach (0: not said) playerClass(uuid) / secondClass(uuid) / race(uuid) String 16 Class, second class and race ids ("mage"), "" for none mobLevel(ref, store, buffer) int 16 A mob's level, on its world thread inPartyWith(one, other) boolean 16 The two players are in one party

sections.title: Levels.Listener events
sections.text: All default methods: override what you need. They run on the thread the leveling mod fires on, so keep them quick. Event Fires when Carries Since levelUp A player's level went up (once, even when several levels were crossed) player, oldLevel, newLevel 14 prestige A player prestiged (Endless Leveling) player, oldPrestige, newPrestige 14 dungeonCleared A dungeon the player was in was cleared player, rank ("E" to "S", "" without) 15 gateCleared A wave gate or fate zone the player fought in was cleared player, rank, waves 15 raidCleared The player finished a raid player, waves 15 raidStarted A raid started for everyone name, world, waves 16 java Copy Levels.listen(new Levels.Listener() { // stopListening in shutdown (or Registrations.onClose) @Override public void levelUp(UUID player, int oldLevel, int newLevel) { ... } @Override public void dungeonCleared(UUID player, String rank) { ... } }); Note With both mods installed only the chosen mod's level-ups and prestige reach listeners, so nothing counts twice. Endless Leveling's dungeons, gates and raids are told either way: only it has them.

sections.title: What Core does with it, and tabs for your plugin
sections.text: Core pays the admin's money per level-up (with a bonus at milestones), gives the placeholders {leveling_level} , {leveling_prestige} , {leveling_xp} and more, raises rewards by level (the level bonus), and shows a "Highest levels" board while a leveling mod runs. Its settings are on three /tempest tabs: Leveling (with either mod), Endless Leveling (only while it runs: prestige, dungeons, gates, raids, mob gold by level, elite mobs) and MMO Skill Tree (only while it runs). Method Since What it does Registrations.levelingTab(tab) 16 A /tempest tab shown only while a leveling mod runs Registrations.endlessTab(tab) 19 A tab shown only while Endless Leveling runs (for what only it has) Registrations.levelingFeature(feature) 16 A town unlock feature offered only while a leveling mod runs Boosts.LEVELING_XP (15) raises leveling XP: Core gives the extra through the mod each time it gives a player XP (Endless Leveling, or MMO Skill Tree in the same skill), so Tempest Events, rank perks and boosters can run "double leveling XP". With both mods installed it raises both. The extra is never boosted again.

sections.title: Skills: Skills
sections.text: MMO Skill Tree's skills, while it runs: one level per skill (Mining, Swords, custom skills too), skill XP, and what happens there. Found by itself, nothing of it is shipped. Works next to Endless Leveling: skills are MMO Skill Tree's own, whichever mod gives "the level". java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 19 && Skills.available()) { int mining = Skills.level(player, "Mining"); // by id or name; 0 when not known yet Map<String, Integer> all = Skills.levels(player); // "MINING" -> 34, ... Skills.giveXp(player, "Mining", 500, "My mod: a task"); // blank skill: the one the admin chose in Core } Method Returns What it does available() boolean MMO Skill Tree runs ids() List<String> The server's skill ids, custom ones too ("MINING", "HERBALISM") name(id) String The skill's name for players ("Mining") find(typed) String The id a typed name or id stands for ("light armor" gives "LIGHT_ARMOR"), "" for none subject(id) String "MINING Mining": the id and name, as in the actions below levels(uuid) Map<String, Integer> Every skill's level, as last read; empty when not known level(uuid, skill) int One skill's level (id or name), 0 when not known giveXp(uuid, skill, amount, reason) boolean Skill XP with the mod's XP banner; false when the mod is not running or the player is offline

sections.title: Its moments, as PlayerActions
sections.text: What players do there is fired as PlayerActions , with the skill, achievement, quest or character after the colon. Tempest Quests counts them as goals; any plugin can. Action (prefix constant) Fires when Amount mmo_skill_level:<id> <name> ( Skills.SKILL_LEVEL ) A skill's level went up The new level mmo_skill_xp:<id> <name> ( Skills.SKILL_XP ) XP from play (not XP Tempest gave) The XP mmo_achievement:<id> ( Skills.ACHIEVEMENT ) An achievement was unlocked 1 mmo_quest:<id> ( Skills.QUEST ) One of its own quests was finished 1 npc_talk:<character id> <aliases> ( Skills.NPC_TALK ) A credited conversation with a character 1 java Copy PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> { if (action.startsWith(Skills.SKILL_LEVEL)) { String skill = action.substring(Skills.SKILL_LEVEL.length()); // "MINING Mining" // ... } }); Note Levels are read when a player joins, every half minute and after every XP gain; a player who has just joined may have none for a moment. Core pays its own skill-level and achievement rewards (the MMO Skill Tree tab), each level and each achievement once ever.

sections.title: Leveling mods for server owners
sections.text: Tempest works with Endless Leveling (by Airijko) and MMO Skill Tree (by Ziggfreed). Nothing of either mod is shipped: Tempest Core finds them through their public APIs within half a minute of the server starting. Without them, nothing changes, and no level requirement ever locks a player out because a mod is missing.

sections.title: One mod, or both
sections.text: Installed What happens Endless Leveling only Its level counts for everything below; its prestige, dungeons, wave gates, raids, classes and mob levels work too MMO Skill Tree only Its skills become one level (total, combat, power level or the highest skill, as you choose); skill and achievement rewards work too Both You choose whose level counts ("Leveling mod" on the Leveling tab). Only that mod's level-ups pay level-up money, so nothing is paid twice. Endless Leveling's dungeons, gates and raids and MMO Skill Tree's skill and achievement rewards keep working. "Double leveling XP" raises both

sections.title: Where to set it: /tempest
sections.text: Every amount starts at 0, which is off: installing a mod changes nothing until you choose. Tab Shown What is on it Leveling With either mod Which mod counts (with "In use: ..."), money per level-up and milestones, the level bonus on other rewards, chat lines, boards, XP boosts Leveling extras With either mod Commands at levels, leveling XP from the economy (daily rewards, crates, contracts, the shop, town projects), levels for paying and gambling (stops alts), town bonuses Endless Leveling Only with Endless Leveling Prestige (money, a command, a bonus), dungeon, gate and raid money, mob gold by mob level, elite mobs MMO Skill Tree Only with MMO Skill Tree Which number is "the level", which skill gets Tempest's XP, money and items per skill level and at milestones, achievement and server-first rewards Pass leveling, PvP leveling, Events leveling With their plugin Pass XP for level-ups (and Endless Leveling clears), PvP rewards by level, events that start with raids (Endless Leveling)

sections.title: What players get
sections.text: Plugin With a leveling mod Core Money for level-ups, commands and items at levels, a bonus on other rewards by level, placeholders and a "Highest levels" board Quests Goals: reach a level; with Endless Leveling also prestige, dungeons, gates, raids and strong mobs; with MMO Skill Tree reach a skill level, gain skill XP, earn achievements, finish its quests, talk to characters. Rewards can give leveling XP (a goal about one skill gives that skill's XP) Shop, Crates, Quests Items, crates and quests that need a level (and with Endless Leveling a class) Pass Pass XP for level-ups; tiers can give leveling XP Jobs Job work gives leveling XP; a job can need a level Contracts PvP rewards for underdogs and fines for bullies, by level Events "Double leveling XP" events; with Endless Leveling community goals for dungeons, gates and raids

sections.title: MMO Skill Tree rewards
sections.text: Reward How it works Money per skill level Paid for every level gained in a skill, more at higher levels; only above the highest level ever paid, so a reset pays nothing again Skill milestones A bonus, items (what does not fit goes to /mail ) and a line for everyone every so many levels Only these skills Limit the rewards to the skills you list Achievements Money per achievement and per achievement point, once each Server firsts A bonus, items and a line for everyone for an achievement only the first player can earn Placeholders: {leveling_level} (the level that counts), {mmo_total_level} , {mmo_combat_level} , {mmo_power} . Note MMO Skill Tree reads a player when they join, every half minute and after every XP gain. A player who has just joined may show no level for a moment.

sections.title: Your own kind of goal
sections.text: java Copy // setup(): admins can now pick "Catch fish" in the editor (/quests, Edit tab) QuestsAPI.registerObjective("fishing:catch", "Catch fish", "Catch", "fish", true, "Fish id or part of it, e.g. Salmon. Empty: any fish."); // whenever a player catches a fish QuestsAPI.progress(playerUuid, "fishing:catch", fishItemId, 1); Goals made with it are kept while your mod is not installed, but they do not count. You can also count the built-in kinds yourself, for example QuestsAPI.progress(uuid, "KILL", "Dragon", 1) for a mob the game does not report.

sections.title: Shipping goals with your mod
sections.text: java Copy QuestsAPI.addGoal(GoalInfo.achievement("fishing:first_catch", "First catch", "Food_Fish_Raw", "fishing:catch", "", 1, 50)); QuestsAPI.addGoal(GoalInfo.quest("fishing:daily", "Daily angler", "Food_Fish_Raw", "fishing:catch", "", 10, 80, "daily")); addGoal does nothing if a goal with that id exists, so it is safe on every start and keeps the admin's changes.

sections.title: Reading progress and hearing about it
sections.text: java Copy QuestsAPI.isDone(uuid, "fishing:first_catch"); QuestsAPI.progressOf(uuid, "fishing:daily"); QuestsAPI.goals(); // every goal, as GoalInfo QuestsAPI.onComplete((uuid, goal) -> { ... }); // after the reward was paid QuestsAPI.givesPassXp(goal.id()); // version 2: false when the admin switched pass XP off for it givesPassXp is new in QuestsAPI.API_VERSION 2; against an older Quests catch NoSuchMethodError and treat it as true.

sections.title: Custom triggers (no new objective needed)
sections.text: Admins can make a goal of the kind Custom trigger and type a name in "Which one", for example visit_shrine . It counts whenever that trigger fires, from any of these: Java: QuestsAPI.trigger(uuid, "visit_shrine", 1) A command (console, admins, other plugins): /questtrigger <player> visit_shrine 1 (permission quests.admin ) A content mod's item, block or NPC: the Quests_Trigger interaction (below)

sections.title: Crates
sections.text: Crates are made by admins in game ( /crates , Edit crates, permission crates.admin ) and saved in universe/mods/crates/crates.json . Each opening is reported as PlayerActions.CRATE_OPEN (amount: the price), which the Quests mod counts for "Open crates" goals; prizes rarer than the admin's threshold are posted to Announcements.BIG_WIN . The price is taken (and can be vetoed) before the prize is drawn. Keys: a crate can need keyAmount of an item ( keyItem ), usually Crate_Key_Bronze , Crate_Key_Silver or Crate_Key_Gold . Give them from other plugins or the console with /cratekey <player> <bronze|silver|gold|item id> <amount> (permission crates.admin ); right-clicking a key opens /crates (page id Crates_Page ). A crate can be locked to a permission ( permission , such as crates.vip ). Prizes can be a permission or a permissions group ("rank"), for some days or for good, given through the server's PermissionsModule and taken back when they run out (unless the player already had them), or a console command with {player} and {uuid} . Crate blocks ( Crate_Block_Wooden , Crate_Block_Iron , Crate_Block_Golden ): which crate each one opens is in universe/mods/crates/places.json (with each crate's last Rare or better win). Admins set it by right-clicking the block (crouch + right-click to change it). The text, circling prizes and floating prizes of openings over them use Holograms (below), which is optional for Crates: without it the lid, sparkles and sounds still play. To use Holograms

sections.title: Holograms: Holograms (Holograms plugin)
sections.text: Floating text, coloured text pictures, floating show-only items and player statues, from any plugin ( Holograms.API_VERSION , 3). Holograms placed through this API have no limit in either edition; the free edition limits only the ones admins place with /holo . Add "AtomicTempest:Holograms": "*" to your manifest's dependencies (or OptionalDependencies , as Crates does) and compile against the Holograms jar (the Maven repository above, compileOnly ). java Copy Hologram sign = Holograms.text("myplugin", world, new Vector3d(10.5, 66, 4.5), List.of(Message.raw("Welcome!"), Message.translation("server.myplugin.sign.hint"))); sign.setLines(...); // players see the new text within a moment sign.moveTo(...); sign.remove(); FloatingItem gem = Holograms.item("myplugin", world, position, "Rock_Gem_Ruby"); gem.glow("#FF4060"); // a coloured light on it (null = none) gem.moveTo(...); // on the world thread it moves at once: call it every tick to animate Statue champion = Holograms.statue("myplugin", worldName, feet, playerUuid); // API_VERSION 2 champion.show(otherUuid); // another player; null shows nobody TextImage banner = Holograms.coloured("myplugin", worldName, feet, () -> List.of(Message.raw("<gradient:#FF4040:#40C0FF>Welcome</gradient>"), Message.raw("&aShop &7open"))); // API_VERSION 3 banner.setSize(1.5f); banner.setFacing(false, yaw); // a fixed yaw instead of facing every player Holograms.texts(); // every plugin's floating text now (API_VERSION 3; /holo menu lists them) Colour

sections.title: Coinflip: CoinflipAPI and RoomMode (Coinflip plugin)
sections.text: Coinflip rooms: a player makes a room with a stake, others join, the coin decides. Add "AtomicTempest:Coinflip": "*" to your manifest's dependencies and compile against the Coinflip jar (the Maven repository above, compileOnly ). java Copy CoinflipAPI flips = CoinflipAPI.get(); // null while Coinflip is not running List<Room> open = flips.rooms(); // open and flipping rooms, oldest first CoinflipAPI.Result made = flips.create(player, CoinflipAPI.COINS_1V1, Bet.coins(500, Side.HEADS)); if (!made.isOk()) player.sendMessage(made.problem()); flips.join(other, made.room().id(), flips.mode(CoinflipAPI.COINS_1V1).matching(made.room(), other.getUuid())); flips.cancel(roomId); // every stake goes back; check who asks first flips.stats(uuid).profit(); // wins, losses, staked, won flips.listen(new CoinflipAPI.Listener() { public void flipped(Room room) { ... } // full: winner fixed, coin in the air public void finished(Room room) { ... room.winner().name() ... room.payout() ... } public void closed(Room room, CoinflipAPI.CloseReason reason) { ... } // CANCELLED, EXPIRED, RESTART }); A Room has an id, its mode, its entries() (player, name, side, value, data; the first made the room), its state ( OPEN , FLIPPING , DONE , CLOSED ), pot() , fee() , payout() , winner() , and the fairness data: hash() from the start, seed() once the coin has landed, roll() once it is full. Provably fair: the seed is 32 random bytes (hex) from SecureRandom ; hash is SHA-256(seed). The roll is the first 13 hex

sections.title: Your own kind of room: RoomMode
sections.text: Coinflip comes with one mode, coins_1v1 . A mode decides what players stake, how many play, how the winner is chosen and how the pot is paid; Coinflip does the rest the same for every mode (the room list, joining and watching, escrow bookkeeping, the fair roll, the animation, the fee setting, stats, news). Item rooms valued by Shop prices, jackpot rooms for many players, private invite-only rooms or tournaments are all modes. java Copy public final class JackpotMode implements RoomMode { public String id() { return "myplugin_jackpot"; } // saved with its rooms public Message title() { return Message.translation("server.myplugin.jackpot"); } public int maxPlayers() { return 8; } public Message describe(Room room) { return Message.raw(Currency.format(room.pot())); } public boolean canSee(Room room, UUID viewer) { return true; } // private rooms: only invited players public Bet matching(Room room, UUID joiner) { return Bet.coins(room.creator().value(), null); } // null: not from the list public Taken take(PlayerRef player, Room room, Bet bet) { // room is null when making a room // check the bet, take the stake; nothing may be kept when refused return Economies.get().withdraw(player.getUuid(), bet.amount(), "Jackpot stake") ? Taken.ok(bet) : Taken.refused(Message.raw("Not enough money")); } public boolean refund(Room room, Room.Entry entry) { // false: tried again later return Economies.get() != null && Economies.get().deposit(entry.player(), entry.value(), "Jackpot refund"); }

sections.title: Jobs: JobsAPI (Jobs plugin)
sections.text: Which jobs there are, who holds them and their levels, and a way for any mod to pay job work Jobs cannot see itself ( JobsAPI.API_VERSION , 2). Declare "AtomicTempest:Jobs": "*" under OptionalDependencies and check JobsAPI.get() != null (null while Jobs is not running). java Copy JobsAPI jobs = JobsAPI.get(); if (jobs != null && jobs.holds(uuid, "miner") && jobs.level(uuid, "miner") >= 10) { ... } jobs.xp(uuid, "miner"); jobs.earned(uuid, "miner"); jobs.earnedToday(uuid); // API 2 // A fishing mod's catch, paid to a "fisher" job the admin made: the level bonus, boosts and caps apply if (jobs != null && JobsAPI.API_VERSION >= 2) { jobs.reward(uuid, "fisher", 3, 5); // false when the player does not hold it; at most 10,000 a call } Core's PlayerActions tells of jobs_paid (amount paid), jobs_level (the new level), jobs_tree (a whole tree felled, 1) and jobs_found (a place found for the first time, 1). sections.title: Town projects: ProjectsAPI (Projects plugin)
sections.text: What is being built and how far each building is, and a word whenever a project changes state ( ProjectsAPI.API_VERSION , 1). Tempest Town uses it to unlock features when a building is finished. Declare "AtomicTempest:Projects": "*" under OptionalDependencies, keep the classes that touch it in one file of their own (as Shop does with Holograms), and check ProjectsAPI.isAvailable() first. java Copy for (ProjectsAPI.Building b : ProjectsAPI.buildings()) { // a copy; empty when Projects is not running b.id(); b.name(); b.prefab(); b.world(); b.state(); b.percentDone(); b.finished(); } ProjectsAPI.building("k3f9"); // one, or null ProjectsAPI.donors("k3f9"); // different players who donated; -1 when there is no such project ProjectsAPI.listen(listener); // listener.changed(building): made, paused, finished, stopped, cancelled, removed ProjectsAPI.stopListening(listener); // in your shutdown() state is the project's state name: CLEARING , OPEN , PAUSED , FINISHING , FINISHED , CANCELLING , STOPPING or STOPPED . sections.title: Integrations with other plugins
sections.text: Set up in /tempest , Integrations tab. VaultUnlocked : when it is installed, Coins registers as its economy, so every VaultUnlocked plugin (player shops, auction houses, jobs, land claims, scoreboards' balance placeholders) uses these coins. Coins are whole numbers: decimal amounts are rounded in the server's favour (charges round up, payments round down), negative and absurd amounts are refused, transfers are all-or-nothing, and wallets cannot be deleted by other plugins. Payments show in wallets and the /eco log under the calling plugin's name. Can be switched off without a restart. Cassaforte : when it is installed, Coins registers as its economy too (the first plugin to register wins, so switch it off in the Integrations tab if another economy should be used). Same rules as VaultUnlocked. Shared banks ( /bank ) are the "shared accounts" of both: VaultUnlocked and Cassaforte plugins can pay into and out of a bank by its name. Banks are kept by Coins in universe/mods/coins/banks . Discord : paste a channel webhook link; jackpots, big wins, lottery winners, achievements and other mods' announcements are posted (each can be switched off). Only real Discord webhook links are accepted, mentions are disabled, Discord formatting in player names is escaped, and messages are sent one at a time (a burst is cut off instead of flooding the channel).

sections.title: Content mods without code (JSON)
sections.text: These interaction types can be used in any item, block or NPC interaction once the plugin is installed: json Copy { "Type": "Coins_Give", "Amount": 50, "Reason": "Found a treasure chest" } { "Type": "Coins_Take", "Amount": 20, "Reason": "Ferry ticket", "Message": "Have a nice trip!" } { "Type": "Quests_Trigger", "Trigger": "visit_shrine", "Amount": 1 } Coins_Give adds coins to the player who used it. Message is optional (otherwise they are told the amount). Coins_Take takes coins, or fails when the player has too little: nothing is taken, the player is told what they need, and the interactions after it in the same chain do not run. Put it before what is being paid for (opening a door, giving an item). Quests_Trigger counts a custom trigger for the player (see above). These run every time the interaction does. For anything that should not be farmed (a reward chest, a shrine), give the interaction a cooldown in your JSON, or have the goal count once (an achievement with amount 1), so a player cannot click it a thousand times. Example: an item that gives a reward once used (in Server/Item/Items/Treasure_Map.json ): json Copy "Interactions": { "Secondary": { "Interactions": [ { "Type": "Coins_Give", "Amount": 100, "Reason": "Treasure map" }, { "Type": "Quests_Trigger", "Trigger": "treasure_map" } ] } }

sections.title: Rules of thumb
sections.text: Check results: withdraw returns false when the player has too little; give nothing in that case. Take first, give second (coins, then items; items, then coins), and pay only for what was really taken. A reward that can be had once (a claim, a finished goal): mark it and write it to disk first, then give it; take the mark back only if giving failed. Two clicks, two pages or a crash in between then never give it twice (Pass, Quests). Keep one lock per thing (a player's data, a room), and call the economy or another plugin while holding it only when no listener can ever wait for that lock: economies call their listeners (Quests, Pass), and a listener waiting for your lock would freeze both. Coinflip takes stakes under its room lock, which nothing else takes; Pass gives rewards after its player lock is let go. Never trust numbers from a page's event data: clamp amounts on the server to what your page offers. Never let something be sold back for more than it costs, and keep coin items out of shops. Never tie coins to real money. Give every coin change a reason. Unregister what you registered (leaderboards, HUD lines, help topics, settings tabs, listeners) in shutdown() . Prefer PlayerActions over parsing wallet reasons: reasons are for people and may change.
